item.text:
Yes. ResStock documents an **unfixed error in Maine’s Geometry Wall Type**, caused by mislabeled county tax assessor data. For example, the reported single-family detached distribution is approximately **10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete/CMU**, which the team confirmed is inconsistent with Maine’s housing stock. The issue report says all published ResStock datasets are believed affected. [Official issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html).

If you need Maine results:

- **Wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use nearby-state ResStock results, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **Measures whose applicability depends on wall type:** reweight Maine results using nearby-state wall type distributions, or use nearby-state results directly. Wood-frame-only insulation measures can otherwise apply to too few Maine homes.

The team does **not currently expect significant impacts on baseline energy consumption, emissions, or bills, or those results where upgrades are applied**, but the investigation remains incomplete. These recommendations and caveats appear in the [issue report’s copy in the specified release corpus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NatLabRockies/buildstock-corpus/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1-v1/processed/resstock/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1/github_site/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.md).
